title: [Performance][KVPool] Reduce AscendStore lookup and save overhead
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Main-branch counterpart of #18837. Long-input AscendStore lookup and non-layerwise save repeatedly expand local HBM hits, walk excluded chunks, and recompute identical reachability masks.

- Mark complete HBM-prefix hashes lazily instead of building local-hit sets for every group. Keep the existing managers' terminal-hash selection and complete-block boundaries.
- Start chunk iteration at the first eligible, addressable block and use `itertools.compress` to select mask-allowed chunks. Preserve short-mask bounds, physical block mapping, NULL filtering, and sharding over eligible candidates.
- Pass store masks directly to the shared iterator, removing the extra mask copy, rewrite, and `any()` scan. Keep loaded-range and durable-save filtering, including rechecking align-state slots that become valid later.
- Reuse reachable masks with a per-coordinator `lru_cache(maxsize=32)`, keyed by aligned length, retention interval, and prompt length. Return copies to isolate callers.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API, configuration, cache-key format, or model-computation changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Ascend A3 hosts 119/120, 32 NPUs: P DP4 x TP4 and D DP16 x TP1; concurrency 49; the same 196 captured chat inputs after four prefix warmups; one output token. Requests use the PD proxy inside the serving container, with the same working communication configuration in all three cases.

| Configuration | Input token/s | Prefill metric token/s | Input loss vs HBM | Prefill loss vs HBM |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| HBM reference | 249359.16 | 5777.35 | 0.00% | 0.00% |
| Installed baseline + pool | 208662.01 | 4810.14 | 16.32% | 16.74% |
| Optimized compatibility port + pool | 242531.18 | 5634.96 | 2.74% | 2.46% |

The optimized port improves input throughput by **16.23%** and the Prefill metric by **17.15%** over the installed pool baseline. Input throughput is input tokens / formal wall-clock span; the Prefill metric is input tokens / summed end-to-end TTFT.

These measurements use a compatibility port on the installed v0.30 runtime, with one formal replay per configuration; they are not a direct benchmark of this main-branch head. Each case completes 196/196 requests and 200 native PD copies with zero transfer failures. P-side external hits are zero, so this comparison measures overhead under local prefix reuse. State-cache warm/cold output consistency remains unresolved in both the installed baseline and optimized port; full-vocabulary logits were not compared.
